title: The Reopening Catalogue
request: For reopening, list the Fern wing's readable books as title and numeric pages, shortest first, preserving ties. Magpies changed the wing labels' case and spaces; bookworms left '?' where a page count should be.
objective: Combine text cleaning, missing-value handling, numeric conversion and stable table sorting.
hints: A tidy name and a readable count are separate checks; neither changes which book the card belongs to.
Use strip and lower for wing labels, exclude '?' before int, then sort the numeric page column.
Build clean wing labels, replace that column, filter readable Fern rows, replace their page counts, and select the two requested columns after sorting.
inputCode:
import random
from datascience import Table, make_array
n = random.randint(4, 9)
names = ['Fern', ' fern ', 'FERN', 'reed', ' Reed ']
titles = make_array(*['Reopening Notebook ' + str(i) for i in range(n)])
wings = make_array(*[random.choice(names) for _ in range(n)])
pages = make_array(*[random.choice(['?', '9', '40', '100', '240']) for _ in range(n)])
shelf = Table().with_columns('title', titles, 'wing', wings, 'pages', pages)
del n, names, titles, wings, pages

fixtures.name: magpies_and_bookworms
fixtures.predicate: any(name != name.strip().lower() for name in shelf.column('wing')) and '?' in shelf.column('pages')

fixtures.name: fern_shelf_closed
fixtures.predicate: not any(name.strip().lower() == 'fern' for name in shelf.column('wing'))

reference:
wings = make_array(*[name.strip().lower() for name in shelf.column('wing')])
clean = shelf.with_columns('wing', wings)
readable = clean.where('wing', 'fern').where('pages', are.not_equal_to('?'))
numbers = make_array(*[int(page) for page in readable.column('pages')])
deliver(readable.with_columns('pages', numbers).sort('pages').select('title', 'pages'))
